knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo=FALSE,warning=FALSE,message=FALSE)

[Start with the concise summary](summary.html).

Mode: **`r run$mode`**. Model: **`r run$config$openai$model`**.
There are **`r nrow(read_csv(file.path(run_dir,"scenarios.csv")))` scenarios**,
one iteration each and no additional validation draws. Pooled candidate counts
are exploratory selection scores; only held-out results enter the outcome tables.
All testing uses alpha/3, while sample-size planning uses alpha/m.

## Study-count recovery

For a measurement with r > 0 true study effects and k reported study discoveries,
credit is k/r if k <= r and zero otherwise. Average equally across measurements
with r > 0. All-null measurements and directional errors are reported separately.
The score evaluates counts, so it can award credit for the wrong studies or signs.
Incomplete target results produce an incomplete score. This single realization
does not estimate long-run error rates or certify any agent's assumptions.

```{r counts}
knitr::kable(counts,digits=4)
```

## Selection decisions

The other two frozen algorithms compete on pooled non-target exposed/control
observations at the same family level. Choose more unique measurement discoveries;
ties use the smaller source index. One surviving candidate is used with a degraded
flag; no surviving candidate produces a failed target. Agents never see these outputs.

```{r decisions}
knitr::kable(decisions)
knitr::kable(candidates)
```

## Frozen scientific explanations

These are the agents' own explanations, displayed as escaped text. Imported
designs retain their original recommendations; pooled selection is a host-side step.

```{r explanations, results='asis'}
for(entry in reports) cat('<h3>',escape_html(entry$label),'</h3><pre>',escape_html(entry$text),'</pre>\n')
```
